note: WHICH SYMBOL a `contains` edge points at is DETERMINISTIC, and it is the DEFINITION. It used to be "whichever the walk pushed first", and push order is not source order — a protocol's methods are symbolized when the protocol is met, so a name with two symbols could land on the later declaration; 667 edges across the three corpora were affected. A definition always displaces a NON-definition, and two things announce a name without defining it. A FORWARD DECLARATION: clojure/core/reducers.clj and gen_math.clj both do `(declare HEADER)` then `(def ^String HEADER …)`, and the edge pointed at the declare, claiming the namespace defines the var where it only PROMISES to; the forward-declaration SYMBOL is still published (the graph needs a node for the call target, and `declare` skips core names entirely), only the EDGE moves. A SPEC ANNOTATION: `(s/fdef my-inc …)` annotates a var that `(defn my-inc [x] …)` defines — same shape, same consequence. Among candidates the EARLIEST declaration line wins, read off source order, so the same input always yields the same edge, which is what makes the class auditable at all.
